{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZh6FPQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDIygc", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 69, "title": "Implement clocked automatic polling for both standard joypads through shared serial state", "body": "## Problem

Automatic joypad polling bypasses the serial protocol implemented by Issue #67. At baseline `80bb25417a08e871d42fef3fb699d23797c8a364`, `SystemBus::tick` snapshots only `buttons` at V=225 and publishes that snapshot after 4,224 master clocks. JOY2–JOY4 always return zero. Automatic polling neither latches nor advances the manual serial registers, so manual/automatic interference cannot occur.

See [controller state and scheduling](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/80bb25417a08e871d42fef3fb699d23797c8a364/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L181), [register handlers](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/80bb25417a08e871d42fef3fb699d23797c8a364/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L310), and [Issue #67’s explicit remaining scope](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/80bb25417a08e871d42fef3fb699d23797c8a364/docs/issue-67-validation.md#scope-and-remaining-limits).

This continues the latest assessment’s recommended prerequisite work. It does not duplicate the completed manual two-pad implementation. The supplied context lists no open Issues.

## Expected outcome

Replace the first-pad snapshot shortcut with scheduled automatic latch/sample/clock activity using the same controller state as manual accesses. Implement one ordinary NTSC polling cycle for two connected standard joypads, with automatic polling enabled before the cycle and kept enabled until completion.

### Hardware contract and evidence prerequisite

Use [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), **SNES Controllers I/O Ports — Manual Reading / Automatic Reading**, and [Anomie’s Register Doc, revision 1157](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), **4200 NMITIMEN**, **4212 HVBJOY**, **4218–421F JOY1–4**, **4016/4017**, and **CONTROLLERS**. The repository’s [reference record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/80bb25417a08e871d42fef3fb699d23797c8a364/docs/issue-67-validation.md#reference-record-read-before-implementation-2026-10-24) documents the shared latch, independent port clocks and standard-pad serial protocol.

Required logical semantics:

- Both ports share the latch; each has independent serial progress. Automatic and manual accesses operate on those same states.
- Standard-pad data is sampled in `B,Y,Select,Start,Up,Down,Left,Right,A,X,L,R,0,0,0,0` order. Completed results place B through R in bits 15–4.
- JOY1 (`$4218–$4219`) receives port 1 Data1; JOY2 (`$421A–$421B`) receives port 2 Data1. JOY3/JOY4 receive the respective Data2 lines, which remain zero for the supported standard pads.
- Input changes after latch release do not rewrite an already captured serial sequence. Manual clocks during a poll affect the selected port’s subsequent automatic samples; manual relatching affects both ports.
- `$4212.0` and result-register visibility follow the polling phases, rather than an unrelated snapshot timer. Polling progresses while CPU execution is held by DMA.

Before choosing timing constants, record a source-backed event table for automatic start relative to VBlank, latch assertion/release, sixteen sample/clock operations, busy assertion/deassertion, result clearing/shifting/publication, and enable sampling. Distinguish source statements, derived expectations and emulator ordering conventions. Include register writes immediately before the start opportunity and after completion; record unresolved mid-cycle enable behavior separately.

**Uncertainty:** the local evidence does not reproduce enough automatic-reading specification text to establish those exact phases. This planner inspected only the repository and supplied context. The existing V=225/H=0 start and atomic end publication are implementation conventions, not independently established requirements. Reconcile the cited specifications during implementation and correct earlier assertions if unsupported; do not preserve a wrong contract merely because tests pass. Unsupported electrical or coincident-edge behavior must remain explicitly unverified.

### Focused scope and non-goals

Implement the ordinary cycle, both result words, shared serial effects, documented busy/result phases, and noncoincident manual interference. Keep existing input APIs and automatic-disabled manual behavior.

Exclude PAL, overscan/interlace scheduling, peripherals/multitaps, frontend multiplayer, physical setup/hold behavior, arbitrary writes exactly coincident with hardware edges, and unresolved mid-cycle enable cancellation/restart semantics. Document these remaining parts without presenting the controller category as complete. Avoid unrelated scheduler refactoring or new test frameworks.

## Context and reproduction

1. Supply pad 1 `$A590` and pad 2 `$5A60` through the existing APIs.
2. Enable automatic polling before VBlank and advance normal emulation until the polling cycle completes.
3. Read `$4218–$421F`.

Expected completed bytes are `[90,A5,60,5A,00,00,00,00]` hexadecimal. Current code returns `[90,A5,00,00,00,00,00,00]`. This counterexample is derived from inspected code; it was not executed during planning.

Existing tests requiring careful preservation or evidence-backed correction include:

- [Manual protocol vectors and original CPU guest](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/80bb25417a08e871d42fef3fb699d23797c8a364/crates/snes-core/tests/joypad_serial.rs).
- `nmi_enable_edge_status_ack_and_autojoy_completion_are_ordered` in `machine.rs`, which currently assumes immediate busy assertion at VBlank.
- [DMA status/result tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/80bb25417a08e871d42fef3fb699d23797c8a364/crates/snes-core/src/machine/dma_tests.rs#L437), including fixtures that directly assign `auto_until`.
- [Original DMA status guest](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/80bb25417a08e871d42fef3fb699d23797c8a364/crates/snes-core/tests/dma_access.rs#L150), whose VBlank-then-busy-clear wait must remain valid if start timing changes.

No tests were rerun during this read-only planning pass.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the specification/event table above, with precise sections and supporting excerpts. Resolve conflicting requirements before encoding expectations. Identify any corrected historical contract and retain honest timing limitations.
- [ ] Implement scheduled two-pad automatic polling through shared latch/serial state. A second independent button snapshot with delayed publication does not satisfy this Issue.
- [ ] Add original independent vectors covering every button on either pad, complementary `$A590/$5A60` and swapped inputs, released/fully pressed pads, ignored input bits 3–0, all eight result bytes, and representative system-bank mirrors.
- [ ] Test immediately before/at/after every documented phase boundary, result visibility during polling, consecutive frames with changed inputs, disabled polling, supported enable transitions, and reset during polling under the existing reset policy. Expected values must come from the documented event table, not production helpers.
- [ ] Test input changes during latch assertion and after release; unequal manual reads of each port during polling; a manual relatch; and manual serial position after completion. Use noncoincident accesses with independently calculated sequences.
- [ ] Demonstrate identical controller outcomes for equivalent fine and irregular clock partitions, including a tick crossing the complete polling interval. Demonstrate natural advancement across DMA and retain prohibited DMA/HDMA controller-read protections.
- [ ] Add an original MIT source-built 65C816 guest using natural CPU scheduling. It enables polling, observes busy start/completion safely, records both pads and Data2 results in WRAM, and checks changed inputs on a subsequent cycle. The host supplies only ROM/buttons and observes results; it must not inject private raster, serial or result state. Enforce instruction/frame deadlines and record source, license and build provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] Demonstrate the second-pad counterexample failing on the recorded baseline and passing after implementation. Preserve existing assertions unless a cited specification correction requires replacement; retain their unrelated coverage.
- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace --locked`. Explicitly report the new automatic suite, `joypad_serial`, `machine::dma_tests`, and `dma_access` results.
- [ ] Run the existing [README hardware gates](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/80bb25417a08e871d42fef3fb699d23797c8a364/README.md#validate): reproduce/compare the original smoke fixture; build pinned tools with `python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc`; run `tools/hardware-tests.py` with the documented ca65/ld65/spcasm paths; and run `tools/ppu-test.py` with the documented bass path.
- [ ] Preserve existing game regressions and provenance. Run `python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py` twice, `npm --prefix web ci`, `npm --prefix web run build`, install Chromium as documented, and `npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'`. Retain mandatory cleared Castle/Memory replays, hashes, assertions and negative controls. Acquire no commercial ROM or firmware.
- [ ] Update README and validation evidence with actual passes, failures and unperformed checks. Limited passing suites establish neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

Inventory remains unchanged in scope and status: **partial** — cpu, bus, scheduler, dma, hdma, controllers, ppu-bg, ppu-offset, ppu-hires, ppu-mode7, ppu-objects, ppu-color, ppu-ports, ppu-display, spc, ipl, dsp-noise, dsp-pitch, dsp-envelope, dsp-echo, dsp-timing; **implemented_unverified** — dsp-voices; **unimplemented** — ppu-raster, pal. All 24 categories remain tracked; none becomes verified through this Issue.

## Optional validation

Physical-controller traces may strengthen unresolved electrical/alignment evidence if already available. They are not mandatory. No additional ROM acquisition is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
